files.description: The files (.shp and .kml) entitled “Least Cost Corridors” contain polygon vector data representing the course of the Least Cost Corridors calculated between toparchies in the kingdom of Herod the Great (excluding waterborne travel). The LCC was determined on the basis of a cost surface based on the digital terrain model of the ASTER mission (spatial resolution of approximately 30 meters; dated to June 13, 2019). The cost surface was calculated based on the degree of slope of the terrain. The cost of movement therefore increases linearly from 1 for flat areas to a theoretical 90 for vertically inclined areas (cliff). The process of determining the lowest cost corridors was performed manually due to the subjective nature of the selected value constituting the boundary of a given lowest cost corridor.
files.label: Least_Cost_Corridors.zip

files.description: The files (.shp and .kml) entitled “Iron Age roads” contain polyline vector data representing the course of Iron Age roads in the Dead Sea catchment area. It was created using archeological data and verified using remote sensing techniques based on high resolution imagery. The native spatial reference of the dataset is WGS-84 (EPSG: 4326). The data contain the following attributes: names of roads, dating, length, width, elevation, minimum Z, maximum Z, mean Z, minimum slope, maximum slope, and average slope.

files.description:
The files (.shp and .kml) entitled “Least Cost Paths” contain polygon vector data representing the course of the Least Cost Paths calculated between toparchies in the kingdom of Herod the Great (excluding waterborne travel). The LCP was determined on the basis of a cost surface based on the digital terrain model of the SRTM mission (spatial resolution of approximately 30 meters). The cost surface (expressed in time [h] needed to travel a pixel) was obtained by calculating the slope of the slopes expressed in degrees (SLOPE_DEM_SRTM), and then converting them according to the formula (in Python) 0.03/(6*Power(math.e, 3.5*Abs(Tan(("SLOPE_DEM_SRTM"*math.pi)/180)+0.05))). The formula was developed based on an equation derived from Gowen KM, de Smet TS (2020) Testing least cost path (LCP) models for travel time and kilocalorie expenditure: Implications for landscape genomics. PLoS ONE 15(9): e0239387. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0239387.
LCPs determined using the Tobler function more reliably reflect the time needed to travel through a raster cell with a given inclination, i.e., the time needed to move increases exponentially, not linearly as in the case of LCPs based directly on the terrain inclination.
files.label: Least_Cost_Paths_Tobler.zip

files.description: The files (.shp and .kml) entitled “Herodian toparchies_2” contain point vector data representing the locations of toparchies during the reign of Herod the Great. It was created using historical and archeological data and verified using remote sensing techniques based on high resolution imagery. The native spatial reference of the dataset is WGS-84 (EPSG: 4326). The data contain the names of toparchies as an attribute. Compared to the files Herodian_ Toparchies_1, the present files do not include double identifications and accounts for the final list of identifications of Herodian toparchies in the project: Thamna is identified as Kh.Tibna, Amathus as Tell Amatha, Livias as Tell el-Hammam, and Bethsaida as Kh. el-Araj.
files.label: Herodian_Toparchies_2.zip

files.description:
The files (.shp and .kml) entitled “Least Cost Paths” contain polygon vector data representing the course of the Least Cost Paths calculated between toparchies in the kingdom of Herod the Great (excluding waterborne travel). The LCP was determined on the basis of a cost surface based on the digital terrain model of the SRTM mission (spatial resolution of approximately 30 meters). The cost surface (expressed in time [h] needed to travel a pixel) was obtained by calculating the slope of the slopes expressed in degrees (SLOPE_DEM_SRTM), and then converting them according to the formula (in Python) 0.03/(6*Power(math.e, 3.5*Abs(Tan(("SLOPE_DEM_SRTM"*math.pi)/180)+0.05))). The formula was developed based on an equation derived from Gowen KM, de Smet TS (2020) Testing least cost path (LCP) models for travel time and kilocalorie expenditure: Implications for landscape genomics. PLoS ONE 15(9): e0239387. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0239387.
LCPs determined using the Tobler function more reliably reflect the time needed to travel through a raster cell with a given inclination, i.e., the time needed to move increases exponentially, not linearly as in the case of LCPs based directly on the terrain inclination.
files.label: Least_Cost_Paths_Tobler.zip
